note: Oracle for the §9 boundary-composition lowering (issue #52). Hand-derived (R-CHAR-3). A caller of a #[boundary]/#[slag] fn that HONORS the callee's contract verifies at L3 THROUGH the assumed contract (the foreign body is external_body — unchecked, L1-enforced at runtime); its assurance_scope is to_boundary (#17). A caller that VIOLATES the callee's req (does not establish it) or OVERCLAIMS its own ens is a COUNTEREXAMPLE, never a false L3 — the composition is sound. external_body is emitted ONLY for the declared boundary/slag fn, never a regular fn.

verifies_to_boundary.name: direct_boundary_caller
verifies_to_boundary.program: #[boundary("ext::ext_id")] fn ext_id(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure ; fn caller(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure { ext_id(x) }
verifies_to_boundary.why: caller establishes ext_id's req (x<100) at the call site and its own ens (result==x) follows from ext_id's ASSUMED ensures -> caller proves L3 through the contract; scope to_boundary via ext_id (the foreign body is trusted-by-fiat, L1-enforced). Was L0 before #52.

transitive.name: transitive_boundary_caller
transitive.program: #[boundary("ext::ext_id")] fn ext_id(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure ; fn g(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure { ext_id(x) } fn h(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure { g(x) }
transitive.why: h -> g -> ext_id: both g and h prove L3 through the contracts; scope to_boundary via ext_id.

counterexample.name: req_violating_caller
counterexample.program: #[boundary("ext::ext_id")] fn ext_id(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure ; fn bad(x: u32) -> u32 req true ens result == x fx pure { ext_id(x) }
counterexample.why: bad's req `true` does NOT establish ext_id's req (x<100) at the call site -> precondition not satisfied -> COUNTEREXAMPLE, never a false L3 (soundness: external_body assumes the ensures but the caller must still discharge the callee's req).
